Description
2026 Australia 1 oz Gold Australian Lunar Series III  Year of the Horse 1oz Gold Bullion Coin  is manufactured by Precious Metal Refiner- Perth Mint, renowned worldwide for its high-end jewelry, precious metal refining services, and investment goods and services. Celebrate 2025 with this magnificent 1 oz Gold coin!!!!
Founded on 20 June 1899, Perth mint is Australia’s most prominent, fully integrated, cutting-edge precious metals company that offers top-quality gold, silver, and platinum goods and services to global markets. Peth Mint is the only government-owned and guaranteed precious metal company in the world run by the Western Australian Government.
The Popular Australian Lunar coin Series, first released in 1996, celebrates the 12 animals of the lunar zodiac. Each animal of the lunar zodiac is said to bestow its dominant characteristics on those born during its rule. The sixth of 12 auspicious animal symbols, the Horse confers wisdom, intelligence, independence, and charm on those born under its influence in 2025, 2013, 2001, 1989, 1977 and every 12th preceding year.
1 oz Australian Gold Lunar coins contains 1 Troy oz of.9999 fine gold comes with mint-strapped boxes of 100, rolls of 20, or protected capsules. Perth Mint backs the weight and purity of the coins. The Australian Lunar Series III Collection from Perth mint continues to carry a long history of minting magnificent bullion coins, including images of animals from the Chinese lunar calendar.
Design of Australian Lunar Series III 2026 Year of the Horse 1oz Gold Bullion Coin
Perth Mint introduced the Lunar III series 3 in 2020. The Year of the Pig, the final year in the cycle, follows the Year of the Mouse, the first year in the Chinese lunar calendar, to conclude each lunar collection at Perth. The Year of the Rabbit is the fourth animal in the cycle, after the mouse, ox, and tiger.
Seventh in line after the snake, the horse is said to bestow independence, charisma, and a sense of adventure on those born under its influence in 2026, 2014, 2002, 1990 and every 12th preceding year. Being passionate and spirited, they are gifted with natural charm and an ability to inspire others.
The coin’s reverse portrays a magnificent horse with elevated hooves displaying strength and poise. The background includes an image of mountainous landscapes and grassland. Included in the design is the Chinese character for ‘Horse’, the inscription ‘HORSE 2026’, and The Perth Mint’s ‘P’ mintmark. The coin’s obverse bears the Dan Thorne effigy of His Majesty King Charles III, as well as the weight, fineness, and the monetary denomination.
